structure: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests is the k6 performance-test suite for INS (dockerStack: null; it runs against the stack, not in it). Layout: src/suites/ (12 *.k6.js entry suites: smoke, peak-day, background-volume, design-target and others), src/k6/ (23 modules, about 4,800 lines: the journey walkers, INS front-door sessions, readiness, eventing, resilience, stub ceilings, reporting), src/config/ (catalogues: journey-endpoints.js names every step's endpoint tags, endpoints.js the endpoint catalogue, smoke.js the journey set bases such as setBase '/live-animals', target.js the target URLs, plus thresholds, traffic and call-ratio config), src/lib/ (helpers: redirects.js parses set roots and create paths, forms.js and form-fill.js fill journey forms, address-book.js), reports/ (generated run output), compose/, scripts/ and a 1,049-line README. Pages are reached by following links and forms from the set root, so routes appear as set bases, create paths, endpoint tags and walker.open calls rather than a route table. The scope is the animals frontend and INS front-door routes the k6 scripts request: the live-animals set root (opened as the animals journey dashboard, which inc-129 stops rendering when the notification list moves to the INS front door), the create path and notification journey pages, and the INS dashboard and address book. Cut in 2 parts along that seam: the animals live-animals journey (about 1,500 lines) and the INS front door (about 1,300 lines). Left out: the high-risk plants journey (src/k6/high-risk-plants.js and the plants steps; journeys.js is shared, and only its live-animals and shared-page behaviour is claimed), load shapes, thresholds, SLAs, stub ceilings, resilience faults, eventing and dead-letter checks, reference-data reads, design-target and generator reporting, src/suites/ wiring, reports/, compose/, scripts/, CI workflows and the *.test.js unit tests (read only to confirm a route, never claimed on their own).

parts.title: Live-animals journey routes
parts.scope: The animals frontend routes the k6 live-animals journey requests: the set root /live-animals opened as the journey dashboard, the dashboard search by reference number, the create path /live-animals/notifications, the notification hub and every live-animals step page in order, documents upload, declaration, confirmation, notification view, amend and cancel-amend, and the backend checks the journey makes. Stops at the INS front door (part 2) and excludes every high-risk plants step.
read: docs/repos/trade-imports-performance-tests.md (workspace page, for context on the journeys)
covers: The live-animals set base '/live-animals' (src/config/smoke.js) and that the journey opens it as the animals dashboard with a crumb, its check text, and its dashboard search by ?referenceNumber= and the 'submitted notification is on the dashboard' check: these are the requests inc-129 breaks
The create path <setBase>/notifications, how the notification id is read from the redirect, and the notification base <setBase>/notifications/<id>

Each of the 13 live-animals steps in STEP_ENDPOINTS order (origin, commodities with its search, consignment-details, identification, import-reason, additional-details, documents with upload and status, addresses with the party picker and its search, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries with add, transporters, contact): the page it opens, the form fields and values it posts, the checks it makes on the response
The shared pages the animals journey requests (hub, notification view, declaration and its save, confirmation, amend, cancel-amend and its save) with their URL matches and checks
The backend requests the journey makes (fulfilments, list by referenceNumber, replace) and the staleAction and identity-sign-in redirect rules in redirects.js
Every page heading, field name, option value or test-data value the scripts assert or post, quoted verbatim

parts.title: INS front-door routes
parts.scope: The INS front-door routes the k6 scripts request: sign-in through Defra ID, the INS dashboard at '/', the dashboard-only session, the returning session that lands back on a dashboard, the nine address-book page requests (list, add, edit, delete), readiness checks against the INS frontend, and the INS read-model and address-book volume reads. Excludes the live-animals journey pages (part 1).
covers: The INS dashboard route '/' (endpoint ins-dashboard), its sign-in hop, and the 'INS dashboard opens signed in' check that the heading is 'Dashboard'
The dashboard-only session and the returning session: which routes they open, and how an expired session goes back through Defra ID to the dashboard

Each of the nine address-book page requests: '/address-book' and its add, '/address-book/<id>/edit' and '/address-book/<id>/delete', with the form fields and values posted and every check on the response, quoted verbatim
The readiness checks that the INS frontend signs in and answers the address book

The INS read-model and address-book reads in background-volume.js, and every INS or animals frontend endpoint name in the endpoints.js catalogue and target URLs in target.js, so each route the suite knows is claimed once (live-animals step endpoints belong to part 1)
